'''Nouria Hernandez''' is a Swiss [[biologist]] and former [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the [[University of Lausanne]].<ref name=Vaud/> She was professor of [[molecular biology]] at the University of Lausanne from 2004 to 2016. She served as rector from 2016<ref name=Vaud/> to 2021.

==Life and career==
Nouria Hernandez studied at the [[University of Geneva]] (diploma in 1980) and received a [[doctorate]] from the [[University of Heidelberg]] (in 1983).<ref name=Vaud/><ref name=Trotta/> From 1983 to 1986, she then worked at the [[Yale University]].<ref name=Vaud/> In 1987, she was nominated group leader at the [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]] and, in 1988, became professor at the [[Watson School of Biological Sciences]].<ref name=Vaud/> In 2004, she moved to Europe and became professor at the [[University of Lausanne]]<ref>{{in lang|fr}} Nadine Richon, [http://www.unil.ch/getactu/wwwcig/1098876240844/ « Deux scientifiques de renom nommés à l'UNIL »], news of the [[University of Lausanne]], 27 October 2004 (page visited on 4 June 2016)</ref> where, between 2005 and 2014, she was also director of the Centre for Integrative Genomics.<ref name=Vaud/> In 2007, she received the [[Cloëtta Prize]]. Between 2008 and 2014, Nouria Hernandez was also a member of the central committee of the [[Swiss Academy of Natural Sciences]].<ref name=Vaud/>

Her research work has focused on the regulation of gene expression in mammals.<ref name="amacad"/> During her PhD, she used an in vitro system to show that the [[Precursor mRNA]] [[Splicing (genetics)|splicing]] reaction could be separated from transcription.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hernandez |first1=Nouria |last2=Keller |first2=Walter |title=Splicing of in vitro synthesized messenger RNA precursors in HeLa cell extracts |journal=Cell |date=November 1983 |volume=35 |issue=1 |pages=89–99 |doi=10.1016/0092-8674(83)90211-8 |pmid=6194902 }}</ref> Afterwards, she worked on the transcription of the U [[small nuclear RNA]]s, which are involved in several cellular processes including [[Precursor mRNA]] [[Splicing (genetics)|splicing]]. This work showed that [[RNA polymerase II]] and [[RNA polymerase III]] transcription depends on several common transcription factors.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hernandez |first1=N |title=TBP, a universal eukaryotic transcription factor? |journal=Genes & Development |date=1 July 1993 |volume=7 |issue=7b |pages=1291–1308 |doi=10.1101/gad.7.7b.1291|doi-access=free |pmid=8330735 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Henry |first1=R.W. |last2=Ford |first2=E. |last3=Mital |first3=R. |last4=Mittal |first4=V. |last5=Hernandez |first5=N. |title=Crossing the Line between RNA Polymerases: Transcription of Human snRNA Genes by RNA Polymerases II and III |journal=Cold Spring Harbor Symposia on Quantitative Biology |date=1 January 1998 |volume=63 |pages=111–120 |doi=10.1101/sqb.1998.63.111 |pmid=10384275 }}</ref> She later worked on the enzyme RNA polymerase III and its effect on transcription in mice when it is deregulated. This led to the discovery of links between RNA polymerase III transcription and the regulation of growth and metabolism, in particular lipid metabolism.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bonhoure |first1=N |last2=Byrnes |first2=A |last3=Moir |first3=RD |last4=Hodroj |first4=W |last5=Preitner |first5=F |last6=Praz |first6=V |last7=Marcelin |first7=G |last8=Chua SC |first8=Jr |last9=Martinez-Lopez |first9=N |last10=Singh |first10=R |last11=Moullan |first11=N |last12=Auwerx |first12=J |last13=Willemin |first13=G |last14=Shah |first14=H |last15=Hartil |first15=K |last16=Vaitheesvaran |first16=B |last17=Kurland |first17=I |last18=Hernandez |first18=N |last19=Willis |first19=IM |title=Loss of the RNA polymerase III repressor MAF1 confers obesity resistance. |journal=Genes & Development |date=1 May 2015 |volume=29 |issue=9 |pages=934–47 |doi=10.1101/gad.258350.115 |pmid=25934505|pmc=4421982 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Willemin |first1=G |last2=Mange |first2=F |last3=Praz |first3=V |last4=Lorrain |first4=S |last5=Cousin |first5=P |last6=Roger |first6=C |last7=Willis |first7=IM |last8=Hernandez |first8=N |title=Contrasting effects of whole-body and hepatocyte-specific deletion of the RNA polymerase III repressor Maf1 in the mouse. |journal=Frontiers in Molecular Biosciences |date=2023 |volume=10 |article-number=1297800 |doi=10.3389/fmolb.2023.1297800 |doi-access=free |pmid=38143800 |pmc=10746880 }}</ref>

In August 2015, after being selected by a vote of the University Council (by 26 votes out of 39) in June, the [[Council of State of Vaud]] nominated Nouria Hernandez as rector of the [[University of Lausanne]] from 1 August 2016.<ref name="Vaud">{{in lang|fr}} [https://web.archive.org/web/20220410140500/https://www.bicweb.vd.ch/communique.aspx?pObjectID=525886 « Le Conseil d'État a désigné la nouvelle rectrice de l'Université de Lausanne »], press release of the [[Council of State of Vaud]], 27 August 2015 (page visited on 4 June 2016).</ref><ref name=24heures>{{in lang|fr}} Renaud Bournoud and Daniel Audétat [http://www.24heures.ch/vaud-regions/unil-rectrice/story/11131212 « L’UNIL choisit une biologiste pour être sa rectrice »], ''[[24 heures (Switzerland)|24 heures]]'', 26 June 2015 (page visited on 4 June 2016).</ref> She was the first woman to lead the University of Lausanne.<ref name=24heures/> As rector, one of her priorities was to promote the theme of "[[viable development]]" (with the idea of survival in the long term of the next generations).<ref name="LT2016">{{in lang|fr}} Olivier Dessibourg [https://www.letemps.ch/sciences/science-une-force-avance-toute-seule « La science est une force qui avance toute seule »], ''[[Le Temps]]'', Saturday 4 June 2016 (page visited on 4 June 2016).</ref><ref>{{in lang|fr}} [http://www.unil.ch/central/home/menuinst/organisation/direction/n-hernandez.html "Nouria Hernandez, rectrice de l'Université de Lausanne"], [[University of Lausanne]] (page visited on 7 August 2016).</ref> She sees viable development as an interdisciplinary subject of reflection involving not only technology but also biology, ecology, philosophy, economy and politics.<ref name=LT2016/><ref>Nadine Richon, [https://podcast.unil.ch/unil/uniscope/622.pdf « Il faut apprendre à créer sa voie »], ''L'uniscope'', campus magazine of the University of Lausanne, number 622, March 2017, pages 4-5.</ref>

In 2023, she received a [[Honorary degree|honorary Doctor of Science degree]] from the [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory|Cold Spring Harbor]] School of Biological Sciences,<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2023 |title=CSHL awards science writer, educator with honorary degrees |url=https://www.cshl.edu/cshl-awards-science-writer-educator-with-honorary-degrees/ |access-date=24 June 2026 |website=Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory}}</ref> and in 2025, she was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="amacad">{{Cite web |date=May 2026 |title=Nouria Hernandez |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/nouria-hernandez |access-date=24 June 2026 |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref>
